items.headline: SIL and digital platform providers must be registered
items.whats_changing: Supported independent living (SIL) and NDIS digital platform providers must be registered with the NDIS Commission.
items.who_it_affects: Providers of SIL and businesses that run NDIS digital platforms.
items.what_to_do: If you deliver SIL or run a digital platform, check your registration covers that service before you deliver it.

items.headline: Claims must be made within 90 days
items.whats_changing: The time to make a claim for an NDIS support drops from 2 years to 90 days after the support is delivered.
items.who_it_affects: Providers, plan managers and self-managing participants who make NDIS claims.
items.what_to_do: Claim each support soon after you deliver it, so nothing is left close to the 90-day limit.

items.headline: Keep payment records for 7 years
items.whats_changing: Providers must keep records of the NDIS payments they receive for 7 years. Not keeping them can lead to a civil penalty.
items.who_it_affects: All providers paid with NDIS funds.
items.what_to_do: Check how long you keep invoices, service records and payment records, and make it at least 7 years.

items.headline: Registration expected to expand to high-risk supports
items.whats_changing: The Government has funded mandatory registration for all high-risk supports, such as personal care. The final list of supports hasn't been published yet.
items.who_it_affects: Unregistered providers of high-risk supports, such as personal care.
items.what_to_do: If you're unregistered and deliver personal care, start preparing for registration now.
